decisions.statement: A service that is not to be running is watched by nothing.
The unit whose health is read is the service unit rather than the timer.
A unit that failed is broken whether or not that service is scheduled.
A service publishing a host name the service could not bind is broken.
A host name unbound is broken whether or not that service is scheduled.
The values a service published beside its page are read from the checkout looked at.
A service is judged by a round of its work only where its page states a window.
A service going longer than its window without a round landing is broken.
A service stating a window and having landed no round at all is broken.
A round overdue is broken whether or not that service is scheduled.
A round overdue is broken though systemd calls the unit active or activating.
A scheduled service resting between its runs is well.
A service that is to be running and has not been for the settle is broken.
A service that stopped running inside the settle is well, a restart taking seconds.
The settle is two minutes, which is longer than any restart a service page states.
A unit systemd says nothing of the moment for waits out no settle.
A unit that failed is broken at once rather than waiting out the settle.
A service still coming up is well rather than broken.
A unit systemd does not know is broken rather than well.
A service reads as broken with the words systemd used.
A unit that failed or is not running names the moment systemd measured it entering that state.
A moment systemd states as no instant is left out rather than guessed at.
systemd is asked about every unit at once rather than about a single unit at a time.
The page a service is stated on is carried with that service's health.
Whether a service is told is carried with that service's health.
A service stating nothing is told.
Nothing here writes a unit or sends a message.

definition: whether the unit each workstation service is installed as is running as it should
